turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sorry we're a little all over the place, the garage was full and then he saw a dog in the lobby and that was the end of walking.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): You're here, that's what counts. I'm Dr. Ellison. What's been going on?
[SEG0003] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Um, Leo's five. He had a cold, and now he's up at night crying and grabbing his ear.
[SEG0004] person_3 (PATIENT): Ow. Ear hurts.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'm sorry, buddy. Can you show me which ear?
[SEG0006] person_3 (PATIENT): Right one. No shots.
[SEG0007] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Right ear, yeah. He gets scared of shots the second we park. It really kicked off three nights ago. Days are cranky, nights are just screaming.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay. Tell me about the cold, however it went.
[SEG0009] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Runny nose, and a little cough, started five-ish days ago. Well, actually the cough is mostly gone. Nose is still drippy in the mornings.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the crying, is that every night?
[SEG0011] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Three nights in a row. He'll be asleep and then around midnight he's just inconsolable, holding that ear.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any fever with this?
[SEG0013] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. I checked last night and this morning. Ninety-eight point four both times.
[SEG0014] person_3 (PATIENT): Hot! Grandma said I was hot!
[SEG0015] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That's my mother. She was over and she kept insisting he felt hot, warm all over. But the thermometer was normal, so I don't think he had a fever. I really don't.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Got it. Two different impressions. Was he pulling at the ear during the day?
[SEG0017] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really. He rubs his cheeks when he's tired anyway.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any pus or drainage from the ear?
[SEG0019] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. I looked with a flashlight like a maniac. Nothing coming out.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Vomiting? Diarrhea?

[SEG0021] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No vomiting. He's eating less than usual. Drinking is, I don't know, I suppose he is, sometimes not really. Mostly apple juice, which his dad says is basically candy, whole other argument.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Breathing okay? Any rash on the skin today?
[SEG0023] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Breathing's been fine. No rash today. Well, actually, I need to ask you about a rash from forever ago before anybody hands me a prescription.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sure, tell me.

[SEG0025] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He had amoxicillin when he was a baby. Long ago. I couldn't tell you when, exactly. And he got a rash, maybe. I think my mom remembers a rash. I don't, not really. So maybe it was the medicine, maybe it wasn't.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): So amoxicillin, possibly a rash, and you're not sure either way.
[SEG0027] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yeah. Please don't write amoxicillin if there's a chance. Is a maybe-rash even an allergy? Could it have been viral? I keep going in circles.
[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): Mommy. Loud.

[SEG0029] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He does that with the TV, says loud, or sometimes that he can't hear it, I honestly can't tell which. Different issue, sorry. Last year at the checkup, he was four, they said his hearing screen was borderline. They told us to repeat it. We never did. I still feel bad.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Borderline on a screen, and no repeat we can use today. I won't treat that as a measured result. Any surgeries, tubes in the ears?
[SEG0031] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No surgeries. No tubes.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): What medicines has he actually taken for this?

[SEG0033] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Tylenol, by mouth, last night, just once. I was gonna say three hundred and twenty milligrams, no, wait, that's not right, I used the children's syringe and I think it was a hundred and sixty milligrams. Maybe. The lines are ridiculous.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): So one dose, possibly a hundred and sixty. Anything else in the house get mixed in?

[SEG0035] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Almost. His dad's metformin was right next to it, five hundred milligrams, for his diabetes. I had the bottle in my hand and then I saw the name. I did not give Leo any of that. Scared me though.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. That one is Dad's, not his. Any other allergies, foods, medicines?

[SEG0037] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No, nothing else that I know of. Um, he lives with me and his dad. Preschool tomorrow is a birthday party and I already ordered cupcakes with dinosaurs, which is irrelevant, but can he even go?
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): We'll land on preschool after I look. Leo, little light for your ears, still no shots.
[SEG0039] person_3 (PATIENT): No shots. Promise?
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Promise. Right ear, thanks for holding still, buddy.

[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right eardrum is a bit red and dull. I don't see bulging, and there's no pus. Left eardrum looks normal. Throat's mildly pink. Lungs are clear. Neck is soft, no stiffness.
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the numbers, since he let me. Temperature ninety-eight point six. Heart rate a hundred and eight. Breathing twenty-four. Oxygen sat ninety-nine percent.
[SEG0043] person_3 (PATIENT): Done?

[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): Done looking. Mom, I think this is probably an early middle ear infection on the right, coming off the cold. It could also just be pressure from the leftover congestion. I wouldn't call it a slam-dunk infection that must be treated this minute.
[SEG0045] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So no antibiotic today? Even with the screaming? What if I'm wrong and it gets bad tonight?
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): Watch and wait today. Pain medicine, and a backup plan so you're not stuck. I don't want to guess with amoxicillin.
[SEG0047] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): What's the backup, exactly? Do I fill something? What if he gets a fever after bedtime?

[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll send cefdinir to your pharmacy. It's a different family from amoxicillin. Don't start it unless a fever shows up, the pain gets worse, or he's not better in two days. If you do start it, it's two hundred and fifty milligrams, five milliliters, by mouth, once a day, for five days.
[SEG0049] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Two-fifty, once a day, five days, only if. Is cefdinir gonna cause a rash too? How fast would I know?
[SEG0050] person_2 (DOCTOR): A rash can happen with any antibiotic. If a new rash shows up after a dose, stop and call. I can't put a number on the odds from a maybe-reaction years ago.
[SEG0051] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Okay. And for the pain, because I don't trust the dose I gave. What should I actually use?

[SEG0052] person_2 (DOCTOR): Children's ibuprofen, by mouth. One hundred and fifty milligrams, that's seven and a half milliliters of the one-hundred-milligram-per-five suspension, every six to eight hours, with a little food. Only if he's hurting. Don't wake him up for it.
[SEG0053] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Hundred and fifty, every six to eight, with food, don't wake him. What if he throws it up?
[SEG0054] person_2 (DOCTOR): Don't repeat a vomited dose. If he can't keep fluids down, call. We're not there now.
[SEG0055] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And his hearing? They said borderline and now this ear. Is it gonna be permanent? Should we have gone back last year?
[SEG0056] person_2 (DOCTOR): Nothing I see today says permanent hearing loss. If he's not better in two days, we might repeat that hearing screen. Not something I'm ordering this afternoon.
[SEG0057] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So the hearing test is a maybe, later. Preschool, the dinosaur cupcakes, yes or no?
[SEG0058] person_2 (DOCTOR): If he's comfortable and there's no fever, he can go. If he's miserable in the morning, keep him home. Your call when you see him.
[SEG0059] person_3 (PATIENT): Dinosaurs.

[SEG0060] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): If he's not better in two days I come back here, right? Not the ER for just crying? Also, sorry, random, that lobby dog had on a sweater. He will narrate that for a week.

[SEG0061] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come back if he's not better in two days. Sweater dog can wait. Middle of the night, if he's hard to wake, the ear starts draining, or his breathing changes, skip the backup plan and go to urgent care or the ER.
[SEG0062] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Hard to wake, drainage, breathing. What about swimming on Thursday? I already paid, which is not your problem.
[SEG0063] person_2 (DOCTOR): Skip the pool until the ear feels normal. A few days won't set him back.
[SEG0064] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Okay, no pool. I think that's everything I had scribbled on the receipt.
[SEG0065] person_2 (DOCTOR): You sorted the important stuff. We'll see him if he's not better in two days. Feel better, Leo.
[SEG0066] person_3 (PATIENT): Bye. Ear still ow.

spec.situation: Mother and a child with ear pain and night crying after a cold; mother says no fever, grandmother says it was hot; mother unsure about the amoxicillin the child had 'long ago, got a rash maybe'; doctor decides on watchful waiting with a back-up plan.
features: spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.

third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
